title: If and when: jodi ... tahole, -le
focus: Conditionals with jodi ... tahole and the -le conditional (brishti hole = if it rains); time clauses.
body:
# If and when: jodi ... tahole, -le

There are two ways to say "if".

**1. jodi ... tahole.** **jodi** means "if" and **tahole** means "then". The if-part uses the ordinary present tense: **jodi tumi jao, tahole ami-o jabo** (if you go, then I'll go too). In speech, **tahole** is often dropped.

**2. The -le form.** Add **-le** to the verb stem and drop jodi: **brishti hole** (if it rains), **tumi gele** (if you go), **somoy pele** (if I get time). It's shorter and very common in Kolkata speech. It works for any person, because the -le form doesn't change.

The -le form also means **when** or **once**: **tumi ele amra cha khabo** (when you come, we'll have tea). The context tells you whether it's "if" or "when".

| Verb | -le form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| hoa (happen, be) | **hole** | brishti hole = if it rains |
| jaoa (go) | **gele** | tumi gele = if you go |
| asha (come) | **ele** | tumi ele = if/when you come |
| paoa (get) | **pele** | somoy pele = if I get time |
| chaoa (want) | **chaile** | tumi chaile = if you want |
| para (can) | **parle** | parle = if I can |
| khaoa (eat) | **khele** | Ollie khele = if/once Ollie eats |
| bola (say) | **bolle** | aste bolle = if you speak slowly |

To say "if not", put **na** before the -le verb: **tumi na gele** (if you don't go).

## Examples

- **kal brishti hole ami jabo na**: if it rains tomorrow, I won't go
- **thanda hole ami barite thakbo**: if it's cold, I'll stay home
- **parle ashbo**: I'll come if I can
- **tumi chaile ami tomake debo**: if you want, I'll give it to you
- **Ollie-ke dekhle amake bolo**: if you see Ollie, tell me
- **tomake jete hole jao**: if you have to go, go
- **tumi aste aste bolle ami bujhte pari**: if you speak slowly, I can understand
- **jodi Ollie-r khide pay, tahole oke khabar dao**: if Ollie is hungry, give him food

## Common mistakes

- ❌ **jodi tumi gele**. Don't combine jodi with -le. Use either ✅ **jodi tumi jao** or ✅ **tumi gele**.
- Don't confuse the -le conditional with the tumi past: **tumi gele** can mean "you went" or "if you go". The second half of the sentence makes it clear.

cards.English: If it rains
cards.Notes: hoa → hole = if (it) happens; lit. 'rain if-happens'

cards.English: If it rains tomorrow, I won't go
cards.Romanization: kal brishti hole ami jabo na
cards.Bengali: কাল বৃষ্টি হলে আমি যাবো না
cards.Notes: brishti hole = if it rains; jabo na = won't go

cards.English: What will happen if it rains?
cards.Notes: hole = if it happens; hobe = will happen

cards.English: If it's cold, I'll stay home
cards.Notes: thanda hole = if it's cold; thakbo = I'll stay

cards.English: If you go, I'll go too
cards.Romanization: jodi tumi jao, tahole ami-o jabo
cards.Bengali: যদি তুমি যাও, তাহলে আমিও যাবো
cards.Notes: jodi = if; tahole = then; ami-o = me too

cards.English: If you don't go, I won't go either
cards.Romanization: tumi na gele ami-o jabo na
cards.Bengali: তুমি না গেলে আমিও যাবো না
cards.Notes: na goes before the -le verb: na gele = if (you) don't go

cards.English: If you want, you can come
cards.Notes: chaoa → chaile = if (you) want; ashte paro = you can come

cards.English: If you want, I'll give it to you
cards.Notes: chaile = if you want; tomake = to you

cards.English: If you want to eat, eat
cards.Notes: khete chai (want to eat) → khete chaile (if want to eat)

cards.English: I'll come if I can
cards.Notes: para → parle = if (I) can; ashbo = I'll come

cards.English: If I get time, I'll come
cards.Notes: somoy (time) + pele (if get); paoa → pe-

cards.English: If it's good, I'll buy it
cards.Notes: bhalo hole = if (it) is good; kinbo = I'll buy

cards.English: If you see Ollie, tell me
cards.Notes: dekhle = if (you) see; Ollie-ke and amake both take -ke

cards.English: If you have to go, go
cards.Notes: tomake jete hobe (you have to go) → jete hole (if you have to go)

cards.English: If you speak slowly, I can understand
cards.Romanization: tumi aste aste bolle ami bujhte pari
cards.Bengali: তুমি আস্তে আস্তে বললে আমি বুঝতে পারি
cards.Notes: bola → bolle = if (you) speak; the l doubles

cards.English: If you come to Kolkata, tell me
cards.Notes: asha → ele = if/when (you) come (irregular)

cards.English: When you come, we'll have tea
cards.Notes: ele = when you come; amra (we) takes -bo like ami

cards.English: Once Ollie eats, he'll sleep
cards.Notes: khele = once/if (he) eats; ghumobe = will sleep

cards.English: If the food is hot, I won't eat
cards.Romanization: khabar-ta gorom hole ami khabo na
cards.Bengali: খাবারটা গরম হলে আমি খাবো না
cards.Notes: gorom hole = if (it) is hot; khabo na = won't eat

cards.English: If Ollie is hungry, give him food
cards.Romanization: jodi Ollie-r khide pay, tahole oke khabar dao
cards.Bengali: যদি অলির খিদে পায়, তাহলে ওকে খাবার দাও
cards.Notes: lit. 'if Ollie's hunger gets, then to-him food give'; oke = (to) him/her
